observation.content: At one declared horizontal station in a synthetic model-boat wave-tank experiment, two undocumented displays simultaneously showed HIGH and LOW.
observation.provenance: Declared synthetic laboratory fixture; no real vessel, instrument, or navigation event is represented

problem_domain: Structural comparison of two undefined measurement labels in a synthetic wave-tank record

competence.rationale: Competence is declared only for identifying missing comparison metadata in the supplied record; no nautical or instrument convention is treated as the undocumented channel definition.

calibration.internal_confidence_rationale: No confidence is assigned to a substantive interpretation because the measurement target and label semantics are undefined.
calibration.external_evidence_rationale: The log supports that the labels occurred, but it does not make their quantities, datums, units, or thresholds comparable.

evidence_sources.description: Synchronized record: model boat at the same horizontal station; display A reported HIGH and display B reported LOW.
evidence_sources.provenance: Synthetic observation log declared by the fixture
evidence_sources.quality_note: Channel definitions, measured quantities, vertical datums, units, thresholds, and label semantics are absent.

assumptions: The declared station fixes only the model's horizontal location, not its vertical coordinate.
The two displays were read at the same synthetic observation time.
HIGH and LOW are arbitrary test-system outputs, not declared nautical standard terms.
No instrument manual, channel map, datum, unit, or threshold definition is supplied.

constraints.description: Do not replace missing channel metadata with a familiar domain convention or an evaluator's preferred interpretation.

hypotheses.statement: The displays measure the same quantity against the same datum and genuinely conflict.
The displays refer to different quantities, such as model elevation and a separate wave or clearance measure.
The displays use different datums, units, or label thresholds for related quantities.
One label describes a physical measurement while the other describes a device or threshold state.

time_horizons.label: After traceable channel metadata becomes available

candidate_actions.description: Suspend treating HIGH and LOW as comparable and request the channel definitions, quantity, axis, datum, unit, thresholds, and experiment protocol.

effects.expected_benefit: No model revision is based on an invented common reference frame.
effects.expected_cost: The apparent conflict remains unresolved during the metadata request.

effects.expected_benefit: The labels can be compared or separated using a traceable measurement definition.
effects.expected_cost: The process requires a new evaluation rather than preserving the initial status automatically.

candidate_actions.rationale: Suspending only the comparison preserves every observed label and every candidate interpretation until a reference frame is documented.
candidate_actions.rollback_cost: Resume comparison and re-run the validator with the documented channel metadata.

items.description: The quantity measured by each display is unknown.
No common vertical datum, unit, or scale is established.
The meanings and thresholds of HIGH and LOW are undocumented.
missing_information: Distinction between measurement and device status

selection_rationale: The reversible selection preserves the recorded outputs without injecting an undocumented reference frame or treating the apparent conflict as resolved.
